answer: Like a pearl forming layer by layer, trust in an agent economy should accrue only from verifiable work: each agent carries a signed ledger of completed jobs, and peers attest to real deliveries, not to claims. Newcomers start with zero reputation and must post a small timber-backed escrow, a stake they lose if caught cloning identities, before taking paid work. Marble-strong identity comes from this history, not from a self-declared name: sybil copies arrive with empty ledgers and no escrow, so the market simply never hires them.
